# Linkedin Jobs Scraper

The Apify actor [`curious_coder/linkedin-jobs-scraper`](https://apify.com/curious_coder/linkedin-jobs-scraper) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **1.7.18**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

Scrape Linkedin jobs from jobs search results using search URLs or filters. Get full job details, job poster and company details.

## Pricing

Pay per event — result $0.002, Actor Start $0.00005 (Free-plan prices; paid plans pay less). Cap the spend with `maxTotalChargeUsd`.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/curious_coder/linkedin-jobs-scraper) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/curious-coder-linkedin-jobs-scraper@1.7.18#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs: {}
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `urls` | array |  | `[]` | Linkedin jobs search URLs — Go to [public linkedin jobs search page](https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/search/) on incognito window (to access public version), search with required filters and once you are done, copy the full URL from address bar and pass it here. You can pass multiple search URLs. When |
| `keywords` | string |  |  | Keywords — Job title, skills, or free-text search (e.g. "software engineer remote"). Used only when the URLs list above is empty. |
| `location` | string |  |  | Location — City, region, or country as you would type it on LinkedIn (e.g. "United States", "London, United Kingdom", "Remote"). |
| `geoId` | string |  |  | Geo ID — Optional LinkedIn geoId for precise location targeting (found in a LinkedIn search URL as `geoId=`). Overrides free-text location when LinkedIn resolves it. |
| `distance` | integer |  |  | Distance (miles) — Search radius in miles around the location. Leave empty for LinkedIn's default. |
| `datePosted` | string |  | `"anyTime"` | Date posted — Only return jobs posted within this window. |
| `companyIds` | array |  | `[]` | Company IDs — LinkedIn numeric company IDs (from a company URL or `f_C=` in a search URL), e.g. "1441" for Google. |
| `under10Applicants` | boolean |  | `false` | Under 10 applicants — Only jobs with fewer than 10 applicants. |
| `autoConvertToAiSearch` | boolean |  | `true` | Auto convert old search URLs to AI search URLs (recommended) — LinkedIn is now forcing AI job search which removed many classic filters (experience, job type, workplace, salary, sort, etc.) When this option is enabled, the filters in old search URLs are converted to natural language and appended to  |
| `scrapeCompany` | boolean |  | `true` | Scrape company details — This will require additional scraping requests for each job record and take longer to scrape |
| `limitPerSource` | integer |  |  | Max jobs per search — Maximum number of jobs to scrape from each input URL (or from the AI search filters when no URLs are provided). Leave empty to scrape as many as LinkedIn returns for each search (up to ~1000). |
| `splitByLocation` | boolean |  | `false` | Split search by city locations — Enable this to split your search by cities within a country. This helps bypass LinkedIn's 1000 job limit per search URL by creating separate searches for each city. This will overwrite the location filter in input search URLs. |
| `splitCountry` | string |  |  | Country to split by — Select the country whose cities will be used to split the search. Only used when 'Split search by city locations' is enabled. Required to when 'Split search by city locations' is enabled. |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
